Maxima exercises

Source: vignettes/maxima.Rmd
maxima.Rmd

Maxima exercises calculate question values and correct answers when an exercise is instantiated. One exported item can therefore produce many random variants. You can write the calculations in a {maxima} chunk, display their outputs with template_value(), and bind a correct answer with gap_numeric(solution_variable = ...) or gap_text(solution_variable = ...).

This article describes the experimental prototype/maxima-rmd branch. Install that version with R >= 4.1, then restart your RStudio R session:

remotes::install_github("shevandrin/rqti", ref = "prototype/maxima-rmd")

Requirements

Install Maxima separately. rqti finds it on PATH, or you can select its executable explicitly:

options(rqti.maxima = "/usr/bin/maxima") # replace with your executable's path

On Windows, use the full path to the command-line launcher, for example:

options(rqti.maxima = "C:/maxima-5.44.0/bin/maxima.bat")

Use your installation’s actual path, including the executable filename. Forward slashes work in Windows R strings. No additional R interface package is required; ordinary rqti exercises do not require Maxima. See Configuration for persistent settings.

rqti runs Maxima locally when checking Rmd chunks and generating previews. An exported exercise needs a delivery platform that supports the ONYX MAXIMA custom operator, such as ONYX/OPAL. The XML retains the program; the sample values from the authoring check are not fixed into the exported question.

Write an Rmd exercise

Here is the complete addition example shipped with this branch:

---
type: gap
identifier: maxima_local_addition
title: "Maxima addition in RStudio"
knit: rqti::render_qtijs
---

<!-- In the RStudio console, run rqti::start_server()
     before clicking Knit. The preview opens in the RStudio Viewer. -->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(rqti)
```

```{maxima addition}
block(
    [a, b, answer],
    a: random(100),
    b: random(100),
    answer: a + b,
    string(['a = a, 'b = b, 'answer = answer])
);
```

# question

What is **`r template_value("a")`** + **`r template_value("b")`**?

Answer: `r gap_numeric(solution_variable="answer", tolerance_type="exact", points=1)`

The Maxima block returns a string containing a named association list: string(['a = a, 'b = b, 'answer = answer]). rqti reads the output names and types from one local execution, creates the template declarations, and keeps the calculation in the QTI template. template_value("a") displays an output; gap_numeric(solution_variable = "answer") uses the generated numeric answer. numericGap(solution_variable = ...) provides the same binding in the S4 API.

Preview in RStudio

Start the preview server in the RStudio console before clicking Knit. Copy the installed example to a writable location first:

library(rqti)
rqti::start_server()
example <- file.path(tempdir(), "maxima-addition.Rmd")
file.copy(
  system.file("extdata", "maxima-local-addition.Rmd", package = "rqti"),
  example,
  overwrite = TRUE
)
rstudioapi::navigateToFile(example)

Click Knit. The RStudio Viewer should show the addition exercise with generated numbers. The preview also works in an external browser using the URL printed by start_server() or render_qtijs().

qti.js sends the template calculation to the local R server, which runs Maxima and returns typed outputs. Submitting an answer preserves the current numbers; reload the preview page to generate another variant. A failed preview shows the diagnostic and a Retry button. To stop the server, use rqti::stop_server().

Output types and authoring checks

Supported output types are integer, float, and string. Rational numbers and real numeric constants can be used as floating-point outputs. Inference observes one random variant; specify types when they may vary between variants:

For example, replace the addition chunk above with this explicitly typed chunk:

```{maxima addition, variables = c(a = "integer", b = "integer", answer = "float", label = "string")}
block(
    [a, b, answer, label],
    a: random(100),
    b: random(100),
    answer: a + b,
    label: "Addition",
    string(['a = a, 'b = b, 'answer = answer, 'label = label])
);
```

The named variables vector sets the QTI types for the returned outputs. answer = "float" accepts both integer and floating-point results. The extra text output can be displayed with template_value("label"). Explicit types do not bypass the local execution check.

Lists and other structured values need an explicit string declaration when used for display.

Text answers

Use gap_text(solution_variable = "answer") when the Maxima output is a string. The output supplies one correct text answer for each attempt; submitting an answer preserves the generated word. Matching ignores case by default; set case_sensitive = TRUE to require matching capitalization. The entire string must match, including spaces and punctuation. Dynamic text answers do not support spelling tolerance or a list of alternative answers. textGap(solution_variable = "answer") provides the same binding in the S4 API.

This example can be previewed in qti.js and exported for ONYX/OPAL:

---
type: gap
identifier: maxima_text_answer
title: "Text answers from Maxima"
knit: rqti::render_qtijs
---

<!-- Run rqti::start_server() in the RStudio console before clicking Knit. -->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(rqti)
```

```{maxima words}
block([answer],
    answer: ["Blue", "Green", "Orange"][random(3) + 1],
    string(['answer = answer])
);
```

# question

The generated word is **`r template_value("answer")`**.

Copy it here (capitalization does not matter):
`r gap_text(solution_variable = "answer", response_identifier = "insensitive")`

Copy it here again (capitalization must match):
`r gap_text(solution_variable = "answer", case_sensitive = TRUE, response_identifier = "sensitive")`

To try it, copy the installed example to a writable location, start the preview server, and open the copy in RStudio:

example <- file.path(tempdir(), "maxima-text-answer.Rmd")
file.copy(
  system.file("extdata", "maxima-text-answer.Rmd", package = "rqti"),
  example,
  overwrite = TRUE
)
rqti::start_server()
rstudioapi::navigateToFile(example)

Click Knit. Copying the word in lowercase earns one point; copying its capitalization exactly into both gaps earns two. Wrong or empty answers earn zero. Submitting preserves the word; reloading generates another variant. Verify generated text-answer scoring in your target LMS before using it in an assessment.

Display LaTeX strings

Return LaTeX as a Maxima string and insert it with template_value(). Double backslashes inside Maxima strings: "\\mathbb{R}" returns \mathbb{R}.

For inline math, surround the reference with \\( and \\) in the Rmd text. For display math, use $$. Alternatively, include the delimiters in the returned Maxima string and insert the reference directly.

The complete example below shows each form. Copy it to an Rmd file, start the preview server, and click Knit:

---
type: gap
identifier: maxima_latex
title: "LaTeX from Maxima"
knit: rqti::render_qtijs
---

<!-- Run rqti::start_server() in the RStudio console before clicking Knit. -->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(rqti)
```

```{maxima latex}
block([],
    string([
        'number_set = "\\mathbb{R}",
        'embedded = "\\(\\mathbb{R}\\)",
        'dollar_embedded = "$$\\mathbb{R}$$"
    ])
);
```

# question

Inline math: \\(`r template_value("number_set")`\\).

Display math:

$$`r template_value("number_set")`$$

Inline delimiters included in the returned string:
`r template_value("embedded")`.

Dollar delimiters included in the returned string:
`r template_value("dollar_embedded")`.

What is $1 + 0$? `r gap_numeric(1, tolerance_type="exact")`

Authoring checks

rqti executes the Maxima chunk before export, including when types are declared explicitly. Errors stop export and identify the source file, chunk, and numbered code. Use one evaluated, uncached Maxima chunk per exercise and return all values needed by the question and answer in its string([...]) list. Related random calculations then share the same execution.

Check Maxima code directly

maxima_check() takes one R character string containing Maxima code, including its terminating semicolons or dollar signs. It runs that code in a fresh local Maxima process and returns TRUE invisibly on success:

rqti::maxima_check("1 + 2;")

For a program returning the same string([...]) associations used in an Rmd chunk, set outputs = TRUE to obtain a named vector of inferred types:

code <- "string(['a = 3, 'answer = 1/2, 'label = \"Addition\"]);"
types <- rqti::maxima_check(code, outputs = TRUE)
types
# c(a = "integer", answer = "float", label = "string")

A syntax or runtime failure raises an R error containing the Maxima diagnostic and numbered source code. Rmd conversion calls this function automatically; you do not need to call it separately before knitting. Execution is bounded by options(rqti.maxima_timeout = 120) in seconds, including library startup. The statistics libraries distrib, descriptive, and stats load by default.

Export and validate 

xml <- rqti::rmd2xml(example, path = tempdir())
result <- rqti::verify_qti(xml, schema = "extended", ignore_import = FALSE)
stopifnot(result$valid)
rqti::rmd2zip(example, path = tempdir())

Choose schema = "extended" for ONYX Maxima items. The standard QTI 2.1 schema rejects ONYX’s customOperator/@value attribute and the setCorrectResponse rule in response processing. The default verify_qti(xml) therefore reports these items as invalid. rqti’s extended schema accepts those extensions while still checking the XML structure.

Schema validation does not execute the Maxima program or prove that every random variant works. Rmd authoring checks run one variant locally; preview scoring and an import into the target ONYX installation provide further checks.

Compiled library cache

The first calculation can take longer while Maxima compiles its libraries. Authoring checks and previews share compiled libraries in rqti’s managed user cache across R sessions. Each calculation still starts a fresh Maxima process; programs, variables, and answers remain independent and temporary.

rqti manages cache cleanup automatically. You can choose another cache directory or keep the cache within the current R session:

options(rqti.maxima_cache_dir = "/path/to/cache")
options(rqti.maxima_cache_dir = FALSE)
